name: Brute Force
description: Adversaries may use brute force techniques to attempt credential access by systematically guessing passwords or cryptographic keys.
detection: Monitor authentication logs for high volumes of failed login events from a single source.

name: Password Guessing
description: Adversaries may systematically guess the password of an account without prior knowledge of system passwords to gain access.
detection: Repeated failed authentication attempts against a single user account from an external or internal source.

name: Password Spraying
description: Adversaries may use a single or small list of commonly used passwords against many different accounts to avoid account lockout thresholds.
detection: Failure events across multiple distinct user accounts from one IP or small CIDR block within a narrow timeframe.

name: Credential Stuffing
description: Adversaries may use credentials obtained from external breach dumps to gain unauthorized access to target enterprise portals.
detection: Distributed login attempts across numerous user accounts originating from residential proxies.

name: Valid Accounts
description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts as a means of gaining Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion.
detection: Inspect unexpected geographic logins, login times outside normal work hours, or unusual access patterns for specific users.

name: Account Manipulation
description: Adversaries may manipulate accounts to maintain access to victim systems, such as modifying credentials, group memberships, or account permissions.
detection: Audit event IDs for group membership changes (e.g. Event ID 4728/4732 in Windows Security logs).

name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism
description: Adversaries may circumvent mechanisms designed to control elevation of privileges to gain higher-level permissions on systems.
detection: Monitor process execution for high integrity levels launched from lower integrity parents.

name: Bypass User Account Control
description: Adversaries may bypass Windows User Account Control (UAC) to run processes with elevated system rights without prompting user consent.
detection: Track registry modifications under HKCU\Software\Classes\ms-settings or auto-elevating binaries.

name: Remote Services
description: Adversaries may use valid accounts to log into a service that is designed to accept remote connections, such as RDP, SSH, or SMB.
detection: Correlate network connection logs on ports 22, 3389, and 445 with user session logins across internal workstations.

name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
description: Adversaries may steal data by transferring it through the existing command and control channel rather than initiating a separate communication pathway.
detection: Monitor network flow metrics for unexpected increases in outbound traffic to established C2 endpoints.

name: Phishing
description: Adversaries may send phishing messages to gain access to victim systems by enticing victims to click links or execute attachments.
detection: Email gateway inspection for malicious URLs, SPF/DKIM validation failures, and suspicious macro-enabled documents.
